- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes in the first 5–7 days of a new 30-day horizon; apply a “warm-up” bias: add 1–2% to forecast for early days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to match sentiment swing direction 1–2 days ahead.
- When sentiment is high and price is near recent high, model often overcorrects downward; apply a “sentiment anchor” rule: if sentiment >0.7 and price >+3% above 14-day moving avg, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
